subject: ba
title: The Organic Business Functions
objectives: Master the four organic business functions: Production, Marketing, Human Resources, and Finance.
Understand the strategic decisions involved in production systems and factory location.
Analyse the marketing mix and the stages of new product development.
Evaluate the scope of human resource management and the core decision areas in finance.
study:
Every business, regardless of size, performs four organic (core) functions that are essential and interdependent — Production, Marketing, Human Resources, and Finance. The word "organic" is deliberate: like the organs of a human body, these functions must work in sync, and a failure in one can bring down the whole enterprise.

Key termProduction — the conversion of raw materials into finished products through certain processes, transforming inputs into outputs that have utility for the consumer.

Production management involves planning, organising, directing and controlling this process. Within it, the production engineer designs the physical equipment, while the production manager organises the use of that equipment and other resources (men, materials, money). Location decisions turn on the availability of labour, transportation, materials and amenities.

Businesses generally choose between three production systems. Job production is small-scale, "one-off" production of a single complete unit to a customer's specific requirements — think custom shipbuilding or bridge construction. Batch production divides work into operations completed for a whole batch before the next operation begins. Flow (mass) production runs continuously, typical of flour mills, breweries, soft drinks and textiles — powerful for volume, but it limits product range and a single technical fault can cause a total breakdown. Quality control runs alongside all three: setting standards, checking conformity, correcting deviations, and driving continuous improvement — inspection happens at incoming materials, mid-process, and as finished goods leave the line.

Exam tipDon't confuse marketing with selling. Marketing is the broader process of moving products from producers to consumers and creating customer satisfaction — selling is only one part of it.

The marketing mix is built from the "4Ps": Product, Price, Place (distribution) and Promotion. Within Product, the "core product" refers to what the buyer is really buying — the fundamental benefit, not the physical item itself. New product development follows a set sequence: idea generation, idea screening (dropping poor ideas early before money is wasted developing them), concept testing, business analysis, product development, market testing, and finally commercialisation.

Human Resource Management treats people as the organisation's most vital asset. Its scope, per E. Flippo, spans procurement, development, compensation, integration, maintenance and separation of human resources — everything from hiring through to exit. The HR department's core roles are staffing, training and development, and industrial relations. A sound HR policy brings real benefits: uniform decisions across the organisation, more confident decision-making, better control, and greater employee confidence.

Finance is critical precisely because Marketing, Production and Personnel all depend on it to function. Financial management centres on three core decisions: the investment decision (which assets the firm should acquire), the financing decision (the best source and method of raising funds), and the dividend decision (how earnings are split between shareholder payouts and reinvestment).
recap:
• Four organic functions: Production, Marketing, Human Resources, Finance — interdependent, like organs in a body.
  • Production systems: Job (one-off, custom) · Batch (whole-batch operations) · Flow/Mass (continuous, high volume).
  • Marketing ≠ selling — marketing is the broader process; selling is one part of it.
  • Marketing mix = 4Ps: Product, Price, Place, Promotion.
  • New product development order: idea generation → screening → concept testing → business analysis → development → market testing → commercialisation.
  • HR scope (Flippo): procurement, development, compensation, integration, maintenance, separation.
  • Finance's 3 core decisions: Investment, Financing, Dividend.

opts: Sports
Astrology
Politics
Finance

quiz.q: Production is best defined as:
opts: The act of selling finished goods to consumers
A synonym for advertising
The process of hiring new staff
The conversion of raw materials into finished products through certain processes

quiz.q: Production Management involves the effort of both the production engineer and the production manager, who:
opts: Only manages the company's marketing budget
Only handles employee payroll
Organises the use of equipment and other resources (men, materials, money)
Only handles government tax filings

quiz.q: Which of the following is a factor influencing factory location, according to the chapter?
opts: Only the founder's personal preference for scenery
Only random selection with no criteria
Availability of labour, transportation, materials and amenities
Only the phase of the moon

quiz.q: Job Production is best described as:
opts: Continuous mass production of identical goods on an assembly line
A synonym for flow production
Small-scale, 'one-off' production of a single complete unit to a customer's specific requirements
A method used exclusively for perishable food items

quiz.q: Batch Production is characterised by:
opts: The complete absence of any specialisation
Continuous flow with zero idle time
Work divided into operations completed for a whole batch before the next operation begins
Producing only one single unique item ever

quiz.q: Flow (Mass) Production is best exemplified by industries such as:
opts: Bespoke tailoring for a single client
Flour mills, breweries, soft drinks and textiles
Bridge construction
Custom shipbuilding

quiz.q: A key disadvantage of Flow Production is that:
opts: It limits the range of products available to consumers, and a technical fault can cause total breakdown
It cannot achieve any economies of scale
It is the most flexible production method available
It always requires highly skilled artisans for each unit

quiz.q: Quality Control aims to establish quality standards, assess conformity, take corrective action and:
opts: Ensure continuous improvement in products and processes
Increase production costs deliberately
Eliminate all forms of inspection entirely
Ignore consumer expectations

quiz.q: Inspection, as part of quality control, occurs at all of the following points EXCEPT:
opts: As finished goods leave the production line
At various stages of the production process
At the shareholders' annual general meeting
At the receiving room for incoming raw materials

quiz.q: Marketing, as distinguished from selling, is best described as:
opts: Identical in scope to selling with no distinction
Only relevant to service companies, not manufacturers
A function unrelated to customer satisfaction
A broader process of activities moving products from producers to consumers and creating customer satisfaction, of which selling is only one part

quiz.q: The Marketing Mix (4Ps) consists of Product, Price, Promotion and:
opts: Profit
Personnel
Politics
Place (Distribution)

quiz.q: Under the Product element of the marketing mix, the 'Core Product' refers to:
opts: What the buyer is really buying (the fundamental benefit)
Only the after-sales warranty
Only the brand name
Only the physical packaging

quiz.q: The first step in New Product Development is:
opts: Commercialisation
Business Analysis
Market Testing
Idea Generation

quiz.q: Idea Screening, in new product development, is important because it helps to:
opts: Guarantee immediate commercialisation of all ideas
Drop poor ideas early, avoiding wasted investment on ideas that would be dropped later anyway
Skip the need for concept testing entirely
Ensure every single idea is developed regardless of quality

quiz.q: According to E. Flippo, Personnel Management involves planning, organising, directing and controlling the procurement, development, compensation, integration, maintenance and:
opts: Production of raw materials
Separation of human resources
Taxation of corporate profits
Marketing of finished products

quiz.q: Which of the following is a role of the Personnel/HR Department?
opts: Staffing the organisation, training and development, and industrial relations
Managing the company's production machinery directly
Setting the company's product pricing strategy exclusively
Filing the company's corporate tax returns exclusively

quiz.q: A key benefit of a sound Human Resources Policy is:
opts: Increased inconsistency in management decisions
Uniform decisions and actions across the organisation
Elimination of the need for any employee records
Guaranteed elimination of all workplace conflict

quiz.q: The Finance function is described as critical because:
opts: Only large companies require a finance function
Marketing, Production and Personnel functions all depend on finance
Finance has no relationship with other business functions
